title: Normalized order of a fraction at a height-one prime
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian normal commutative domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a height-one prime and let $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak q}$ be the existing length order on ring elements of [def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group], computed in $R_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For $x\in K$, take the standard fraction presentation $(a,b)=\operatorname{IsLocalization.sec}(x)$, where $b$ is a nonzero divisor and $x\,b=a$, and define $v_{\mathfrak q}(x)=\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak q}(a)-\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak q}(b)\in\mathbf Z$. For $x\ne0$ this is the normalized additive valuation of the discrete valuation ring $R_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]: both local orders are finite and their difference is independent of the fraction presentation. No valuation property at $x=0$ is asserted.
